description: R0-35-EXIT-PROOF binds the two R0-13 family suites no manifest bound: contacts-import-write-scope.integration.test.ts (created by the R0-13-CT-PERSISTENCE-PROOF repair 965fa631, extended by R0-13b-CT-IMPORT-ACTOR) and ops-scope-command-procurement.integration.test.ts (created by R0-13g-OPS-SCOPE-COMMAND-PROCUREMENT at 3f81d016, the follow-up to R0-13f's revived procurement routes, D-40). Every case that passed at the R0-35 head is required (50 cases); allowAdditionalCases is true so a later packet may add a case without editing this manifest, while a required case that is renamed, skipped, turned into a todo or deleted rejects the verdict, and a new skip or todo fails release0-proof-coverage.spec.ts until scripts/proof-admission/release0-index.json explains it. Run from the repo root: node scripts/proof-admission/run-manifests.mjs --only contacts-import-ops-scope.json (or pnpm --filter server proof:release0 for every Release 0 manifest), against a migrated isolated database and REDIS_URL.
requiredCases: fixture sanity (real rows) seeded one tenant with an owner, four STAFF members and eight live contacts, and no import traces

NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none cannot import contacts POST import/image/ocr by STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none answers 403 and writes no contact, event, audit entry or media; POST /contacts by the same member is refused alike

NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none cannot import contacts POST import/file (csv) by STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none answers 403 and creates no import job, import row, contact, event or audit entry

NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none cannot import contacts import/link (global fetch stood in for two fixed URLs) POST import/link by STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none answers 403 before the link is fetched, and creates no import job or contact

NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none cannot import contacts POST import/scan by STAFF with crm write but crm_edit none answers 403 before the vision model is called, and writes nothing

a 409 from an import route names the existing holder only when the importing member can open it NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF (view all, edit any) importing the email of the owner's PRIVATE contact through import/image/ocr gets 409 with existingContactId null; the holder is untouched, and the same member's GET of it answers 404

a 409 from an import route names the existing holder only when the importing member can open it STAFF with crm_edit owned importing the email of a TEAM contact it can open but not edit gets 409 naming that contact; the holder is untouched, and the same member's GET of it answers 200

an import row that matches an existing contact merges into it only when the importing member may edit that contact NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF (view all, edit any) importing a CSV whose rows match a TEAM contact and the owner's PRIVATE contact: the TEAM contact is merged, the PRIVATE one is left exactly as it was and its row FAILED without naming it

an import row that matches an existing contact merges into it only when the importing member may edit that contact NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF with crm_edit owned importing a CSV whose rows match its own contact and the owner's TEAM contact: its own contact is merged, the owner's is left exactly as it was and its row FAILED
positive control: an OWNER import still works through every route POST import/image/ocr by the owner answers 201 and creates the contact, its media row and its events

positive control: an OWNER import still works through every route POST import/file (csv) by the owner answers 201 COMPLETED: new rows are created and a row matching a PRIVATE contact the owner may edit is merged into it

positive control: an OWNER import still works through every route import/link (global fetch stood in for two fixed URLs) POST import/link by the owner answers 201 COMPLETED and creates a contact per row
positive control: an OWNER import still works through every route POST import/scan by the owner answers 201 and creates the extracted contact

SYSTEM CONTEXT: findOrCreateContact takes the actor as an explicit argument; callers that pass none keep their behaviour REGRESSION CONTROL: the public booking call shape (bookings.service.ts, no actor) still merges into a PRIVATE contact by email and creates a new contact, tenant-scoped only

SYSTEM CONTEXT: findOrCreateContact takes the actor as an explicit argument; callers that pass none keep their behaviour NEGATIVE CONTROL: findOrCreateContact(businessId, input, actor) applies that actor: crm_edit none is refused 403 with nothing written, and a PRIVATE holder the actor cannot open is neither merged nor named

a member whose CRM reach is limited to owned contacts owns what an import creates, so re-importing merges instead of colliding (review repair CR-1, ST-3) STAFF with crm_edit owned: import/image/ocr of the same new card twice answers 201 both times with the same contact, owned by that member

a member whose CRM reach is limited to owned contacts owns what an import creates, so re-importing merges instead of colliding (review repair CR-1, ST-3) STAFF with crm_edit owned: a CSV with two rows of the same new email answers 201 COMPLETED 2/2; one contact, owned by that member, with both rows linked to it

a member whose CRM reach is limited to owned contacts owns what an import creates, so re-importing merges instead of colliding (review repair CR-1, ST-3) STAFF 'my book' (crm_view owned, crm_edit owned): a card it imports is owned by it, its GET of that contact answers 200, and importing the card again merges into it

a member whose CRM reach is limited to owned contacts owns what an import creates, so re-importing merges instead of colliding (review repair CR-1, ST-3) STAFF with crm_edit owned: a name-only card imported twice within five minutes resolves to one contact

a member whose CRM reach is limited to owned contacts owns what an import creates, so re-importing merges instead of colliding (review repair CR-1, ST-3) positive control: STAFF who may edit every contact it sees (view all, edit any) leaves an imported contact without an owner, as before, and re-importing it merges into it

an import records the importing member as the actor, as POST /contacts does (review repair ST-2) a contact a STAFF member creates through import/image/ocr: its contact.created and contact.imported_from_media events and its created audit entry name that member

an import records the importing member as the actor, as POST /contacts does (review repair ST-2) a STAFF CSV row merged into the owner's TEAM contact writes an 'updated' audit entry naming the member with the fields it filled, and its contact.imported event names the member

an import records the importing member as the actor, as POST /contacts does (review repair ST-2) regression control: findOrCreateContact with no actor (system context) attributes no member: the contact.created event has no actor, the created audit entry names SYSTEM, and a merge writes no audit entry

import/link settles each row on its own: a refused row is FAILED and the rest of the file is imported (review repair CR-2) NEGATIVE CONTROL: STAFF (view all, edit any) importing a link whose middle row matches the owner's PRIVATE contact: 201, the import FAILED with 2 of 3 rows processed, the other two rows created and linked, the refused row FAILED without naming the holder, and the holder untouched

import/link settles each row on its own: a refused row is FAILED and the rest of the file is imported (review repair CR-2) STAFF with crm_edit owned importing a link with two rows of the same new email: 201 COMPLETED 2/2, one contact owned by that member, both rows linked to it

GET imports/:importId/records lists a row linked to a contact only to a member who may open that contact (review repair ST-4) NEGATIVE CONTROL: the owner's CSV row merged into the owner's PRIVATE contact is listed to the owner and to no STAFF member; its row linked to a new TEAM contact is listed to a view-all member and not to a 'my book' member

GET imports/:importId/records lists a row linked to a contact only to a member who may open that contact (review repair ST-4) positive control: a member sees every row of its own import, the created row linked to its contact and the refused row (FAILED, linked to no contact)

route census: command.controller.ts, procurement.controller.ts and business-command-center.controller.ts [OPS-C01] RED-BEFORE: every CommandController and ProcurementController route runs behind AuthGuard, BusinessGuard and then ModuleScopeGuard and requires 'operations' on its handler: read for a GET, write for every mutation (approve, reject, issue-po and invoice included)

route census: command.controller.ts, procurement.controller.ts and business-command-center.controller.ts [OPS-C02] the census is complete: the routes Nest finds on the three controllers are exactly the routes this suite sends over HTTP, at the level the table names; a route added to any of them fails here until it is listed (and refused below to a member without operations)

route census: command.controller.ts, procurement.controller.ts and business-command-center.controller.ts [OPS-C03] the cockpit snapshot is the named exception: it runs behind AuthGuard, BusinessGuard and ModuleScopeGuard with no module requirement; any other route on business-command-center.controller.ts must carry operations like the rest

route census: command.controller.ts, procurement.controller.ts and business-command-center.controller.ts [OPS-C04] the census reader sees class and method guards and the handler scope, and flags an undecorated route (anti-vacuity)

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-01] fixture: seven bizA members (OWNER and ADMIN on role defaults, STAFF with no operations key, operations none, read, role default and write) and bizB with its own owner, one active supplier connection each

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-02] RED-BEFORE: a STAFF member whose scope map has no operations key, and one whose map says operations 'none', gets 403 (operations requires read or write) on every command-centre item route (items list, due, read, create, PATCH, bulk complete, dismiss and delete, dismiss, snooze, approve, execute, complete, discharge, assign, reopen, DELETE, generate, summary, last-scan, auto-scan) and nothing is written

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-03] RED-BEFORE: the same two members get 403 on every procurement route (list, create, suppliers, stats, read, PATCH, submit, approve, reject, vendor, issue-po, acknowledge, fulfill, invoice) and nothing is written: no request changes, no purchase order is issued

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-04] RED-BEFORE: operations 'read' (an explicit grant, and a STAFF member on role defaults) lists and reads every command-centre and procurement GET (200) but every mutation answers 403 (operations requires write, you have read) and nothing is written

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-05] operations 'write' reaches every command-centre and procurement route (GET 200, PATCH and DELETE 200, POST 201; procurement approve and reject 201 since FOLLOW3-D15, RED-BEFORE 500): the gate refuses on scope, not on role

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-06] OWNER and ADMIN (role defaults, operations admin) keep every route, the cockpit snapshot included (procurement approve and reject 201 since FOLLOW3-D15, RED-BEFORE 500)

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-07] refusal: an unauthenticated caller gets 401 and another tenant's owner 403 on every route of the three controllers, and nothing is written

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-08] the cockpit snapshot stays open to a member without operations (the census's named exception): the STAFF member with no operations key and the one with operations 'none' read it 200, as release0-journey's step 5 STAFF member does

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-09] review SEC-R013g-2: a member of bizA the gate admits (STAFF operations write, and the OWNER) who sends another tenant's command item or procurement request id through bizA's own path gets 404 on every route that takes an id (the single-item routes, the bulk bodies, PATCH, submit, approve, reject, vendor, issue-po, acknowledge, fulfill, invoice) and bizB's rows are unchanged. This harness arms no TenantInterceptor, so the route's own binding is what is proven: acknowledge, fulfill and invoice look the request up in the path business before the transition, as submit and vendor do

the operations gate over HTTP (real guards, real rows) [OPS-10] review SEC-R013g-1 / CR-1: KEY reaches a command or procurement tool only where HTTP admits the same member: the position envelope (JobRolePolicyService.envelopeForPosition, bounded by the holder's real membership row) gives no command_* or procurement_* tool to the members the gate refuses and only the read tools to operations read; the legacy 'procurement' family key reaches none of them. RED-BEFORE FOLLOW3-D15 (PR-03): the three procurement vendor transitions, whose service writes now bind the business, are operations write: an operations:write envelope reaches them, operations:read and the members HTTP refuses do not

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-11] RED-BEFORE PR-01: ProcurementService called directly (no HTTP request, no TenantInterceptor armed: how the KEY staff bridge calls it) with bizA's business id and bizB's request id refuses every write with NotFound, and bizB's row is byte-identical: update, submitForReview, updateStatus (approve and reject), selectVendor, issuePO, acknowledgeVendor, markFulfilled and markInvoiced; no purchase order, no audit row and no feed row is written

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-12] RED-BEFORE PR-01: every write ProcurementService makes to a procurement request is an updateMany whose where names { id, businessId } and is refused (NotFound) unless it moved exactly one row; each of the eight writing methods writes through one; none writes approvedAt, approvedByUserId, rejectedAt, rejectedByUserId or rejectionReason, which the model does not have

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-13] RED-BEFORE PR-02: POST procurement/businesses/A/:id/approve (the OWNER, and a STAFF member with operations write) answers 201 with status APPROVED, the row is APPROVED, and exactly one BusinessEvent records the decision: business A, subject procurement_request :id, action approved, the approving member as the (human) actor, the status before and after; the Activity feed row is still written and names the approver

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-14] RED-BEFORE PR-02: POST procurement/businesses/A/:id/reject with a reason answers 201 with status REJECTED, and exactly one BusinessEvent records the decision with the reason in its metadata (action rejected, the rejecting member as actor); the Activity feed row is still written and carries the reason

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-15] a refused or failed approve or reject writes no BusinessEvent: refused by the gate (unauthenticated 401; STAFF operations read, no operations key, another tenant's owner 403) or failed (bizB's request through bizA's path, 404, as the OWNER), the request is unchanged and no audit, feed or other row is written

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-16] review SEC-D15-1 / CR-D15-1: an update that names no field answers the request as it is (200), not 'Request not found': PATCH {} and a PATCH whose only key the whitelist strips ({ notes }), as a STAFF member with operations write and as the OWNER, and the KEY procurement_update_request call that sends neither priority nor internalNotes; nothing is written. The business binding holds: the same empty update of bizB's request through bizA is still 404 / NotFound and bizB's row is byte-identical

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-17] review SEC-D15-3: PATCH cannot decide a request: a body that sets status APPROVED or REJECTED (any case) answers 400 for a member with operations write and the OWNER, the request is byte-identical and no audit row is written; the decision is made only through approve and reject, which record it. A foreign request still answers 404 first, and a PATCH that sets any other status or field still writes

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-18] review SEC-D15-2: a decision is a compare-and-set on the status it read. When another decision lands between updateStatus's read and its write, the later one is refused (ConflictException, 409), writes no audit or feed row and leaves the first decision standing; and under real concurrency (approve and reject of the same SUBMITTED request at once, 10 times) every audit row records the status its own call wrote, the rows chain (the first starts at SUBMITTED, each starts where the previous ended), the request ends at the last row's status, and every call that wrote nothing was refused as a conflict

FOLLOW3-D15-PROCUREMENT-BOUND-WRITES (V1-84): ProcurementService binds the business on every write; approve and reject decide and are audited [OPS-19] review SEC-D15-4: a decision stands only with its audit row. When the audit insert fails (Postgres refuses a NUL character: a reject over HTTP whose reason holds one, and an approve called directly whose actor id holds one), the call answers 503 / ServiceUnavailableException, the request is byte-identical (still SUBMITTED) and no audit row, feed row or bus event is written; the same reject with a clean reason then decides it with exactly one audit row
